newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends firmer but most gains pared.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends firmer but most gains pared.

text.p: CSCE cocoa ended firmer ahead of the U.S. cocoa grind data due Friday, but most of the gains were pared as the initial surge fizzled, traders said.
Higher-than-expected issues on Thursday's first notice day in the May contract was seen as bullish by some traders, helping to spur the initial surge in spot May to a high of $1,452 per tonne.
Some of the momentum spilled over into most-active July, pushing the contract to a high of $1,480 per tonne.
But from mid-morning the upward surge began to fizzle and the market went into a long, slow retreat. May ended $18 firmer at $1,418 while July went out $12 higher at $1,451.
Traders said trade buying provoked commission house, fund and speculative interest which triggered buy stops to fuel the run-up, following on from Wednesday's technicall-based buying.

Friday's U.S. first quarter cocoa grind, due before the market opens, is not expected to spring any surprises, with the market expecting the data to be in line or a little higher than the same period last year.
